notation.x0: The separate initialization parameter; hseq forces x(0)=x0.
notation.D: Dψ(first argument, second argument), derivative at the second argument.
notation.toReal: EReal.toReal is a total map: a finite embedded r maps to r, while both +∞ and −∞ map to 0. Thus the displayed real differences are not an unrestricted extended-real subtraction. For t<T, P(ℓ_t) together with the global supporting-vector condition on V forces ℓ_t to be finite on V. Reachability places x_{t+1} in V and u∈V, so these particular positive-horizon summands use finite values. No finiteness of ℓ_t(x0), or of values outside V, is asserted.

P.domain: An extended-real function f:E→ℝ∪{−∞,+∞} on a compatible carrier.
P.expansion: P(f) \iff [\forall z\in E,\ f(z)\ne-\infty]\ \land\ [\exists z\in E\ \exists r\in\mathbb R,\ f(z)=r].
P.meaning: No value is −∞, and at least one value is finite. Other values may be +∞. This is not global real-valuedness, boundedness, continuity, or convexity.

C.domain: An extended-real function on a topological carrier E.
C.expansion: C(f)\iff \forall r\in\mathbb R,\ \{z\in E:f(z)\le r\}\text{ is closed}.
C.meaning: Only real sublevel thresholds are quantified. It does not assert convexity or finite values.

S.domain: f:E→EReal and x∈E, with E a real complete inner product space in this packet.
S.expansion: S(f,x)=\{g\in E:\forall y\in E,\ f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle\le f(y)\}.
S.meaning: The finite real inner product is embedded in EReal before addition and comparison. The test ranges over all E, not only V. Nonemptiness at z means ∃g, followed by ∀y; g may depend on z and on the loss index. Combined with P(f), nonemptiness at z forces f(z) finite, because the finite witness in P rules out f(z)=+∞.

D.domain: ψ:E→ℝ, x,y∈E, on a real normed space with the structures required by fderiv.
D.meaning: The derivative is taken at the second argument and applied to first minus second. This is a total definition: Lean's fderiv is the zero continuous linear map where the function is not Fréchet differentiable. No differentiability, convexity, positivity, symmetry, or coercivity is a premise of the definition itself.

A.domain: V⊆E, ψ:E→ℝ, η∈ℝ, f:E→EReal, x∈E; output Option E.
A.expansion: Q_{\eta,f,x}(z)=f(z)+\iota(\eta^{-1}D_\psi(z,x)),\qquad W=\{p\in E:p\in V\ \land\ \forall z\in V,\ Q_{\eta,f,x}(p)\le Q_{\eta,f,x}(z)\}. \quad A(V,\psi,\eta,f,x)=\begin{cases}\mathrm{some}(\operatorname{choose}(W\ne\varnothing)),&W\ne\varnothing,\\ \mathrm{none},&W=\varnothing.\end{cases}
A.meaning: ι embeds a real into EReal. Membership p∈V is explicitly required in addition to IsMinOn. The chosen point is a noncomputable classical witness. This definition does not prove a minimizer exists or is unique, nor require a finite minimum. If all objective values on a nonempty V are +∞, every point of V can satisfy the displayed minimization predicate. No η>0 assumption is built in; real inversion is total, with 0⁻¹=0.

I.domain: V⊆E, ψ:E→ℝ, η:ℕ→ℝ, loss:ℕ→E→EReal, x0∈E; output ℕ→Option E.
I.meaning: The update from t to t+1 uses loss t and η t. Initial membership x0∈V is not checked. A failed update makes every later value none. Reaching some(x_t) is a premise or concrete conjunct, not an unconditional guarantee. An arbitrary sequence of minimizers need not equal this particular classical-choice sequence.

∀z∈ℝ, f1(z)≠−∞, and ∃z∈ℝ ∃r∈ℝ, f1(z)=r. Here z=0,r=0 is a finite witness.
\forall z\in[-1,1]\ \exists g\in\mathbb R\ \forall y\in\mathbb R,\quad |z|+g(y-z)\le f_0(y). Equivalently the test is |z|+g(y−z)≤|y| for every y∈[−1,1]; outside that interval the right side is +∞.
∀z∈[−1,1] ∃g∈ℝ ∀y∈ℝ, (−5/4 z)+g(y−z)≤f1(y). Equivalently this is (−5/4 z)+g(y−z)≤−5/4 y for all y∈[−1,1]; outside V the right side is +∞.
\forall r\in\mathbb R,\quad \{z\in\mathbb R:z^4/4+z^2/2\le r\}\text{ is closed}.
\mathbb R\text{ is convex, and }\forall a\ne b\in\mathbb R\ \forall\alpha,\beta>0,\ \alpha+\beta=1\Rightarrow \psi(\alpha a+\beta b)<\alpha\psi(a)+\beta\psi(b).
ψ is DifferentiableOn ℝ on all ℝ, equivalently differentiable at every real point.

I_0=\mathrm{some}(1/2),\ I_1=\mathrm{some}(0),\ I_2=\mathrm{some}(1/2). The actual classical-choice A updates return 0 and 1/2. The first objective on V is |z|+Dψ(z,1/2); the second is −5z/4+2Dψ(z,0), because η1⁻¹=2.

seven_slots.constants_normalization: The second loss slope is −5/4, twice the item_5 slope, and its step is 1/2. The second movement is consequently weighted by 2. At u=−1/2, R6=−7/4 and the retained-terminal bound is −29/64. At u=1/2, R6=−1/2 and both displayed right sides equal 2(9/64)−29/64=−11/64, since the terminal divergence is zero. These substitutions explain the numerical conjuncts without adding a new theorem claim.
seven_slots.probability_feedback_semantics: Entirely deterministic. There is no probability space, random variable, expectation, high-probability event, sampling rule, filtration, measurability, independence, unbiasedness, bandit feedback, or oracle model. The left side uses ℓ_t(x_{t+1}), evaluated after the update using ℓ_t, minus ℓ_t(u). No bound for ℓ_t(x_t) is stated. A consumes the entire loss function as a mathematical argument; no implementable feedback access guarantee follows.
boundaries: The maximum contains previous states x0 and x1, not terminal x2. Here x2 happens to equal x0, which does not change the stated index set.
Only reachability through 2 is asserted. The total schedule and x definitions do not certify future reachability.
The positive and monotone schedule conditions in the conjunction concern the used range only, despite the given schedule itself being globally positive and nonincreasing.
C concerns only the embedded regularizer. No uniqueness, arbitrary-input existence, or probabilistic assertion is a conjunct.
This reconstruction expands the proposition and simplifies arithmetic; it does not inspect or validate any Lean proof.

semantic_findings: All five general interfaces are conditional on finite-horizon reachability of a partial, noncomputable classical-choice recursion.
Items 0,1,2 contain no convexity assumption on ψ and retain signed expressions. Item 0 has no monotonic-schedule hypothesis.
Only items 2 and 4 require T>0. Their monotonicity compares adjacent used steps, and their last divisor is η(T−1).
The explicit M in item 2 and the finite maximum in item 4 cover previous states t<T, excluding terminal x_T.
Items 3 and 4 add V⊆X and strict convexity of ψ on X. They omit the terminal divergence but retain movement subtraction.
The supporting-vector test is global in y; with P it ensures losses are finite on V, despite total EReal.toReal mapping infinities to zero.
The concrete interfaces contain respectively sixteen and twenty-two top-level conjuncts. Their negative numerical right sides and movement constants are preserved.
No interface gives stochastic or bandit-feedback semantics, and no statement alone certifies proof correctness.
